findings.title: Billable count does not filter out inactive projects
findings.explanation: The query counts every row in `projects` for the org. The neighbouring `activeProjectNames` function implies that projects have an active/inactive state (archived, deleted or similar), and that this query filters on it. This one does not, so archived or soft-deleted projects would be billed. Since this number feeds invoices, that means overcharging customers. Apply the same predicate as `activeProjectNames`, ideally through a shared constant or helper so the two cannot drift apart. If archived projects really are billable, document that decision in the code and the PR description.

findings.title: Billing definition of 'billable project' is not specified or tested
findings.explanation: The PR adds no tests. Pricing logic should have tests covering at least an org with no projects, an org with archived or deleted projects, and an org with only active projects. The PR description should also say which project states are billable, for example whether trial, demo or free-tier projects count, and whether the count is taken at invoice time or as a period snapshot or peak. A live count at invoice time can differ from what the customer used during the billing period.

findings.title: Comment mentions Business plan, but the function is plan-agnostic
findings.explanation: The function counts projects for any org regardless of plan. Either rename or reword the comment so callers do not assume the plan check happens here, or leave the plan gating explicitly to the invoice generator.
